We have \begin{align*} 4 r^2 & = x^2 + y^2 + z^2 \\ & = \left( x + y + z \right)^2 - 2 \cdot \left( xy + yz + zx \right) \\ & = \left( x + y + z \right)^2 - 54 . \end{align*}

Therefore, we solve the following constrained optimization problem: \begin{align*} \max_{x,y,z} \ & x + y + z \\ \mbox{subject to } & (1), (2) \end{align*}

Solution 2a (Implicit differentiation)[edit]

The method of Lagrangian Multipliers is fundamentally derived from implicit differentiation, allowing us to bypass the auxiliary multipliers entirely.

We treat the system of constraints as a -dimensional curve in , parameterized by , where and .

As with the above solution, the problem is equivalent to maximizing the function subject to and .

At the maximum along the constraint curve, the total derivative with respect to must vanish: \begin{align*} \frac{d}{dx}(x+y+z) &= 1 + y' + z' = 0 \tag{1}\\ \end{align*}

Differentiating both constraint equations with respect to gives: \begin{align} \frac{d}{dx}(xy+yz+zx) &= (y+z) + (x+z)y' + (x+y)z' = 0 \tag{2} \\ \frac{d}{dx}(xyz) &= yz + xz y' + xy z' = 0 \tag{3} \end{align}
